text:
By Jahna Michal ,
5 hours ago
South Jersey just got hit with another round of snow, and if you‚Äôve been white-knuckling your commute, you‚Äôre not alone. Slippery roads mean drivers are (hopefully) being a little more cautious this week. Honestly, there‚Äôs never been a better time to be extra careful.
In New Jersey, a single at-fault accident doesn‚Äôt just ruin your day, it can wreck your budget for years.
New Jersey Ranks #2 For Post-Accident Insurance Hikes According to a new study from LendingTree, New Jersey drivers face the second-largest increase in car insurance premiums nationwide after causing an accident.
The numbers are eye-opening. On average, Garden State drivers pay an extra $5,998.92 in car insurance over three years following an at-fault crash. That‚Äôs the second-highest dollar increase in the country.
READ MORE: The 5 Most Dangerous Places To Take Selfies In NJ Percentage-wise, it‚Äôs just as painful. Premiums jump 62.7% after an at-fault car accident . That‚Äôs a staggering 17.7% higher than the national average.
READ MORE: Why South Jersey Travelers Love Flying Out Of ACY If you‚Äôre a younger driver, the financial hit is even worse. A 20-year-old in New Jersey pays an average of $2,024 more per year after an at-fault accident. That‚Äôs not exactly spare change.
Canva Snowy Roads, Serious Consequences With winter weather sticking around, this is your reminder that safe driving isn‚Äôt just about avoiding injuries. It‚Äôs about protecting your wallet, too.
Download the WPUR Mobile App Now Take it slow. Leave extra space. Maybe skip that risky lane change today. You shouldn‚Äôt be in that much of a hurry. In New Jersey, a few seconds of impatience can cost you thousands.
The 10 Most Stolen Vehicles In New Jersey Gallery Credit: Jeff Deminski Photo by Robin Mathlener on Unsplash Ford Econoline E250 These are cargo vans commonly used for work vehicles. I can‚Äôt tell you how many of these I drove doing delivery jobs between radio gigs. Not much to look at but pure function. In 2020 158 of these were stolen in New Jersey. Photo by Jessica Furtney on Unsplash Toyota Corolla 184 were taken by thieves in Jersey last year. Part of the reason for thefts of older model Corollas is their quality catalytic converters and Toyota recently began a marking program to reduce thefts. Photo by Jessy Smith on Unsplash Ford Econoline E350 New Jersey saw 199 of these beasts stolen in 2020. Since these work vehicles are almost always hauling something I wonder what other freebies the thieves got. Photo by Kushan Pancholi on Unsplash Honda CRV Some say Honda CRVs are desirable to thieves for their catalytic converters. The part that contains precious metals is easier to access on certain cars of certain model years. In New Jersey 229 were reported stolen in 2020. Photo by Kevin Bonilla on Unsplash Toyota Camry Should we convince Kylie Moore that deer she hit with her Camry in August was trying to carjack her? After all it‚Äôs the sixth most commonly stolen vehicle in New Jersey with 274 taken last year. Photo by Rebecca Lane on Unsplash Nissan Altima These are well made cars that can last between 250,000 and 300,000 miles. Not if a Jersey thief has their way. 277 were taken in 2020. Photo by Kirk Thornton on Unsplash Jeep Cherokee/Grand Cherokee Earlier this year the Cherokee Nation formally asked Jeep to stop using the name for their Cherokees and Grand Cherokees. Their principal chief, Chuck Hoskin Jr., said, ‚ÄúI‚Äôm sure this comes from a place that is well-intended, but it does not honor us by having our name plastered on the side of a car.‚Äù Would they be more honored to know it‚Äôs the 4th most coveted car in the Garden State? 336 taken in 2020. Photo by Muhammad Amaan on Unsplash Ford pickup (full size) 425 of these were stolen last year. Did all those 150s lose their truck nutz at the scene of the crime or were they taken too? Photo by Hung Pham on Unsplash Honda Civic You didn‚Äôt think there would be only one Honda on this list did you? Of course the make rounds out the top two with the Civic in second place. 457 stolen in the Dirty Jerz last year. Photo by Igor Stepanov on Unsplash Honda Accord 541 stolen. Why is it so often the most stolen car? Because it‚Äôs such a reliable car, it‚Äôs a top-selling car. With so many in the road, the more that get in accidents the more that need repair. Stealing an Accord for parts can be far more lucrative than stealing other cars as there‚Äôs such a high parts demand. 9 times cars crashed through perfectly stationary buildings in NJ Gallery Credit: Jeff Deminski Getty Images This video store in South Jersey Back in 2012 law enforcement said a fairly new video store called Play n‚Äô Trade was the scene of an out of control vehicle coming straight through the wall. Luckily it was 10:30 p.m. and employees had locked up for the night. The driver was okay. Henry Mandel/ Townsquare Media of the Hudson Valley This Jersey City mini mart In April of 2021 a Toyota RAV4 ended up entirely inside the mini mart of a gas station in Jersey City according to city officials. No serious injuries and hey, at least they didn‚Äôt hit any gas pumps on the way in. Townsquare Media This Target in Cherry Hill Maybe you shouldn‚Äôt name yourself Target if you don‚Äôt want to be treated like one?
According to Target an ‚Äúelderly guest‚Äù drove right through the side and police say ended up entirely inside the store. Three minor injuries in the February 2021 crash. Getty Images This Pathmark in Irvington What happened in this March 2019 crash seems to be caused by a medical emergency.
A driver saying they had chest pains lost control of a car and plowed through the glass windows of a Pathmark store resulting in three injuries according to police. Getty Images This comic book store in Scotch Plains According to authorities, in October of 2021 a driver under the influence drove his car into a street lamp then halfway inside the front of Little Shop Of Comics.
People living in the upstairs section above the shop were displaced due to structural integrity. This Wendy‚Äôs in South Brunswick This car doesn‚Äôt actually penetrate the wall of the building but the surveillance videos are so terrifying that it had to be included.
In August of 2021 on Route 130 in South Brunswick a driver lost control of her car and went over a berm and went airborne, finally crashing like a rocket from the sky into this fast food restaurant, according to authorities.
Miraculously only the driver needed medical care. Wanamassa Fire Company This unlucky house in Ocean Township Hit me once shame on you. Hit me twice, well, in this case, shame on both of you. It certainly wasn‚Äôt this Ocean Township home‚Äôs fault it was hit twice by two separate cars 8 days apart in January of 2022.
In the second incident police say the vehicle wound up entirely inside the home. Only minor injuries in the incidents. maximkabb This house on Christmas Eve Is Santa supposed to deliver this way?
A home in Hillsborough that was fortunately unoccupied at the time had a Honda Odyssey minivan crash through the wall and end up partly in the garage and partly in the living room according to police.
Police say the incident, which happened on Christmas Eve 2021, was the result of an intoxicated driver in a stolen minivan. This home in Egg Harbor City In November of 2021 a dump truck went out of control across a field and barreled into the home of an 80-year-old man in Egg Harbor City, authorities say.
The damage was so severe it collapsed the floor of the living room where the elderly man was sitting and he fell into the basement, yet neither that man nor the driver were seriously injured according to police. 1
